pairs.subject: frame-direction
pairs.evidence: lib/motion/direction.ts:115 The motion-direction turn reads only the rendered plate (no beat, no function) and asks for up to three independently moving elements as an image-to-video prompt that is stored in FrameClip.motion, so the move can be neither one semantic change nor the beat's argument, and the intent field is filled with renderer prompt text.

techniques.evidence: lib/motion/direction.ts:115 Up to three element moves per frame breaks the one-move rule. directMotion's only input is the plate (line 226), so rule 4 (let the move carry the beat's argument) cannot hold. Line 91 frames the output as 'the text prompt for an image-to-video model', which is renderer configuration and not medium-independent intent. A decline leaves the field empty instead of authoring stillness. Text bans (line 116) and camera-move filtering do conform.
lib/ads/types.ts:140 An ad shot's super is its own field and is drawn by code at Finish, never by the image model. The image line (line 137) carries only the picture.

lib/ads/validate.ts:23 The ad scenarios validator refuses the whole round on any shot finding and lists every finding per shot. The round is a first generation with no earlier content and its shots are coupled by rung structure, so the technique's own exception applies: batch the fixes before applying anything. It is not a direction pass over existing frames. Separately, line 546 rejects duration words in motion, which the technique's restraint list forbids (see registryProposal).

pairs.registryProposal: Two techniques disagree on durations in motion text. per-beat-rejection lists 'no duration or easing vocabulary checks' among the things a validator must not enforce. motion-intent-authoring bans durations in motion text ('no durations, no frame rates, no easing vocabulary'), and a defect that is measurable by construction is exactly what per-beat-rejection says to enforce. lib/ads/validate.ts:546 enforces the ban and is right by one technique and wrong by the other. The standard should say which one wins.
